answer: Coordination Depth Pricing. An agent's vote costs more when it joins a large, tight cluster: price scales with the count of distinct members whose actions correlate above a threshold over a short window. Costly clusters form a river of expensive ballots, so a sybil swarm must pay superlinear total fees to match an honest minority. Isolated agents trade cheaply, a calm oasis of low-fee coordination, while the broad ocean of routine activity stays affordable. Attackers bear rising marginal cost per added identity.
